jobs.occupation: Baker – Bakery Production – Maribo, Lolland, Denmark
jobs.description:
Dansk version længere nede

Den Gamle Bagergaard in Maribo is looking for a baker. You do not need a formal qualification if you have practical experience working in a bakery.

We are a family-run business with three bakers and a pastry chef in production. Two packing staff and a driver help get our bread ready and delivered to our shops.

Your work

You will take part in the daily production at the bakery. We are looking for someone who knows their way around a bakery, takes responsibility for their work and enjoys working with colleagues. You must be able to communicate in Danish or understandable English.

You must already have the legal right to work in Denmark, for example through EU/EEA or Swiss citizenship or a valid Danish residence and work permit. We cannot offer visa or work permit sponsorship.

What we offer

• 
Gross monthly salary: Based on qualifications and experience. For a qualified baker, the salary starts at approximately DKK 26,000.

• 
Permanent, full-time employment

• 
Pension scheme

• 
5 weeks of vacation

• 
Flexible benefits account

• 
Additional pay for applicable night and Sunday work

• 
The employer can support you in finding accommodation in the area

The planned working hours start at 01:30 on Mondays and 05:00 from Tuesday to Thursday. You will also work every other weekend. During the night shifts on Mondays and every other weekend, you will bake bread, Danish pastries and other baked goods. We will agree on the schedule together, and working night shifts only is also an option.

The expected start date is 1 November 2026.

Recruitment process

The first interview can be held online if needed. Selected candidates may be invited to visit the bakery before a final employment agreement is made.

We review applications as they arrive, so please apply as soon as possible.

How to apply

Send your application and CV to rekruttering@lolland.dk with “Baker – Maribo” in the subject line.

If you have questions, contact Martin Hansen, Business Consultant and EURES Adviser at Lolland Municipality, on +45 21 47 73 43 or maha@lolland.dk.

We kindly ask recruitment agencies and intermediaries to refrain from contacting us regarding this position. Applications will only be considered if submitted directly by candidates.

About Lolland and relocation support

Lolland is in southern Denmark and offers easy access to nature, beaches and open countryside, along with affordable housing and short commuting distances. The region is developing rapidly, partly due to the Femern Belt Fixed Link between Denmark and Germany.

If you are moving from abroad, Lolland Municipality’s Newcomers Service can help with practical questions about relocation, registration, housing, a partner’s job search and settling in Denmark. Read more at newcomers.lolland.dk. You can also find information about working in Denmark at workindenmark.dk.

Fast fuldtidsstilling

Send din ansøgning og dit CV til rekruttering@lolland.dk, og skriv “Bager – Maribo” i emnefeltet.

jobs.occupation: Chef to join our international kitchen team
jobs.description:
CHEF WANTED FOR STAFF RESTAURANT IN COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

Looking for a chef position in Copenhagen with great working hours, professional cooking and weekends mostly free?

We are looking for a skilled and motivated chef to join our international kitchen team in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Your main workplace will be The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine, located at Kalvebod Brygge in central Copenhagen.

This is a full-time position with working hours primarily Monday to Friday from 06:30 to 14:30 – giving you the opportunity to work in an ambitious professional kitchen while still having your afternoons, evenings and most weekends free.

Occasional evening and weekend events may occur.

THE JOB

You will become part of a professional kitchen team responsible for the daily production and service at our staff restaurant.

We cook from scratch and care about good ingredients, seasonality, flavour and proper craftsmanship.

You will work primarily with hot kitchen production and take responsibility for your own preparation and tasks while working closely with the rest of the team.

Our kitchen is busy, so we are looking for someone who works efficiently and in an organised manner without compromising quality.

Just as importantly, we are looking for a good colleague.

We believe a professional kitchen should be a place where people communicate respectfully, help each other and enjoy coming to work.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

You may already be living in Denmark, or you may be considering moving to Copenhagen from another EU/EEA country.

We would like to hear from you if you:

• 
are a trained chef or have equivalent professional kitchen experience

• 
have experience from à la carte restaurants, quality staff restaurants, hotels or similar professional kitchens

• 
have solid experience in the hot kitchen

• 
have a genuine interest in food, ingredients and good craftsmanship

• 
can organise your own work and maintain a good pace throughout the day

• 
are reliable and comfortable starting work early

• 
enjoy working as part of a team

• 
communicate in a positive and respectful way

• 
can maintain an overview when the kitchen gets busy.

A background in classic French or Mediterranean cuisine would be particularly relevant to our kitchen.

However, we are also interested in chefs who bring their own culinary background and experience. Whether your inspiration comes from France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Greece, North or South America, Asia or somewhere else, we would like to see what you can bring to the team.

We want to taste what you are passionate about.

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a full-time chef position in central Copenhagen with a working schedule that is unusual in the restaurant industry:

Monday–Friday
Primarily 06:30–14:30
Most evenings and weekends free

You will join a friendly and international workplace with experienced colleagues, high professional standards and room to contribute your own knowledge and ideas.

We value professional pride, teamwork, reliability and a positive working environment.

Our goal is simple: good food, good ingredients, good craftsmanship and a kitchen team that works well together.

MORE THAN A STAFF RESTAURANT

Your daily workplace will be:

The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine
Kalvebod Brygge 35
1560 Copenhagen V
Denmark

Our kitchen also produces food for our small Copenhagen wine bar, Sankt Annæ 8, located in Christianshavn.

Within the same ownership group, we operate several Copenhagen restaurants, including Le Métier, La Propina and Ma Cuisine.

You will therefore become part of a wider restaurant family with different concepts and opportunities for future professional development.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION

Position: Chef
Employment: Full-time
Working hours: Primarily Monday–Friday, 06:30–14:30
Workplace: Copenhagen, Denmark
Starting date: As soon as possible / by agreement
Salary: Based on qualifications and experience and agreed individually
Evening/weekend work: Occasional events only

INTERESTED?

Send us your CV and a short application in English to:

job@willworkforfood.dk

Please write “CHEF FOR ABACUS” in the subject line.

Tell us a little about yourself, your kitchen experience, what kind of food you enjoy cooking and when you would be available to start.

Applications are reviewed continuously, and suitable candidates will be invited for an interview.

If you are currently living outside Denmark, please mention your current location and when you would potentially be available to relocate to Copenhagen.

We look forward to meeting you for a coffee and a conversation about food, ambitions and your future in Copenhagen.

The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine
Copenhagen, Denmark

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Clinical Pharmacy
jobs.description:
Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy, and Environmental Medicine at the Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health, University of Southern Denmark, is offering a new 5-year (20%) position for an Associate Professor within clinical pharmacy. The position is to be filled from February 1st, 2027.

The academic position

The research areas of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM) span from pharmacological epidemiology to clinical studies and cell-based basic pharmacology. CPPEM has a strong background in investigations of exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. The academic position is affiliated with the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, that utilizes the Danish registries to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. 

The area of research is flexible within the area of pharmacoepidemiologic and clinical research and could be (but is not limited to) drug use patterns and rational pharmacotherapy. The department has a strong focus on interdisciplinary collaboration both in-house and with external researchers and the new person is expected to continue this tradition.
 

Areas of responsibility

The applicant will be expected to establish their own research area within the pharmacoepidemiologic research group at the department. Thus, the applicant should be able to attract external research funding to support research and employ scientific and technical staff. The applicant may have a background within pharmacy or medicine.

The research unit teaches in four educations: Medicine, Pharmacy, Chiropractor, and Biomedicine, and the position comes with teaching obligations within these subjects at the University as well as supervision of bachelor and master projects. Additionally, we expect that you will contribute to administrative duties, e.g., participating in Study Board or other similar activities. 

Fluent English (both written and spoken) is required. You are expected to have qualifications that renders it probable that you will be able to establish your own research area within the research unit. Further, you are required to have a PhD degree or similar research experience. 
 

Employers

Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine today has approximately 50 employees. It consists of three separate research groups: pharmacoepidemiology, translational pharmacology, and environmental medicine. Additionally, it collaborates closely with the Department of Pharmacology at OUH. Collectively, this constitutes Denmark’s largest center for research, teaching and clinical service in pharmacology.

It produces approximately 100 international peer-reviewed publications per year. 

Professor Tore B. Stage heads the unit and Professor Pernille Tanggaard Andersen heads the Department.

Management

The Associate Professor answers to the research leader for the unit of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine.
 

Contact information

Further information can be obtained from the leader for the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, Professor Anton Pottegård (apottegaard@health.sdu.dk).
 

Application deadline and interviews

November 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CET
 

Salary and terms of employment

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Applications will be assessed by an expert committee. Applicants will be informed of their assessment by the university.

Applications – including the required attachments – must be sent via the below-mentioned link “Apply online". Only online applications will be accepted. Attached files must be Adobe PDF or Word format. Each field in the application form can contain up to max. 10 MB.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.
 

Application (as pdf- or Word/docx- files):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (inclusive of PhD diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please notice that one pdf- or docx- file must be attached for each publication

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

References will be obtained for the applicant who is the first choice for the position – from the applicant’s most recent employer and previous employers as required.

Further particulars concerning the application – please see the link below.
 

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark is a world-class university driven by an ambition to promote research results that develop society. The major challenges of the 21st century are complex and multifaceted; sustainable change and solutions require new – often interdisciplinary – research-based knowledge, and the University of Southern Denmark is an indispensable stakeholder in the transition process. 

Value, quality, talented people and outstanding environments are pivotal for the University of Southern Denmark’s strategic initiatives. 

Read more: https://www.sdu.dk/en/om_sdu

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship at the Danish Institute for International Studies
jobs.description:
PhD scholarship at the Danish Institute for International Studies, Military Artificial Intelligence, Peace and International Security

The Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS) is recruiting a PhD candidate to research military applications of artificial intelligence and their implications for peace and international security. We are especially interested in projects that examine how the development and use of AI-based military capabilities affect established practices of decision-making, human control, and accountability. The project should connect a nuanced understanding of the dynamics of technological change to wider questions of arms control and international regulation. 

The position is based at the DIIS Centre for Peace Research and will thematically be placed under one of the three pillars of the Centre, namely Arms control in a time of arms races and war. One of the questions that the Centre focuses on is how Nordic countries, including Denmark, can navigate a situation where the development of new technologies (e.g. AI and drones), along with increasing great power rivalry and competition in space, entail new types of security risks that traditional arms control models and treaties do not effectively regulate.

The successful candidate will develop an independent PhD project that speaks to the overall focus of the center and produces research relevant to Nordic and international debates on security and peace.

About the position 
AI is changing how military organizations collect information, assess threats, select targets and coordinate operations. These capabilities are currently developed faster than military doctrine, legal interpretation and oversight arrangements intended to govern their use. This raises questions about who exercises control, how responsibility is assigned, and how other states interpret capabilities whose operation is difficult to observe. Within this overall frame relevant proposals may examine:

• 
The relationship between the adoption of AI and the development of military doctrine

• 
The effects of AI-enabled decision support on military decision-making and the human role therein

• 
The impact of uncertainty and opacity around the current state of AI integration among militaries on escalation dynamics and arms-race dynamics

• 
Regulation of AI through multilateral governance mechanisms in and beyond the UN

• 
Human judgement and accountability in military applications of AI

About DIIS and the position
The successful candidate will be employed by DIIS in a three-year, full-time PhD position, expected to commence on 1 February 2027. The candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), while their primary place of work will be the Centre for Peace Research at DIIS.

The PhD project will be jointly supervised by a senior researcher at DIIS and Professor Ingvild Bode at SDU.

At DIIS, the PhD candidate will join an inspiring and ambitious research environment committed to advancing multidisciplinary scholarship. The successful candidate is expected to engage actively in cross-disciplinary collaboration and to value insights from colleagues working with different theoretical and methodological approaches. Such exchanges across disciplinary boundaries are central to the research environment at DIIS.

We expect the candidate to:

• 
have obtained a master’s degree in a relevant field

• 
have at least received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master’s thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale and a high weighted grade point average 

• 
meet the general requirements for being accepted for enrolment as a PhD candidate (see below)

• 
live up to the DIIS entry criteria for PhD positions https://www.diis.dk/files/media/document/diis-entry-criteria-rev-okt-24.pdf 

• 
communicate clearly in written and spoken English, and proficiency in Danish is an advantage.

DIIS as a workplace
We offer an attractive and inclusive workplace where our employees can develop. We consider knowledge sharing and feedback essential to creating a dynamic workplace. We expect you to participate proactively in the common efforts of the institute. We prioritize a high degree of presence but want our employees to have a good work-life balance. Therefore, we offer flexible working hours and some possibility of working from home. We are located very close to Copenhagen’s city center with excellent public transportation options.

DIIS is a diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for this position regardless of their personal background. DIIS is also a workplace where we consider the environmental consequences of our activities and strive to adopt more environmentally sustainable practices both in relation to our daily business at DIIS and our global travel activities.

In the assessment, consideration will be given to the following criteria:

• 
The applicant has a relevant master’s degree or equivalent qualifications (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process), cf. the Danish qualifications framework for higher education

• 
Quality and relevance of the project description

• 
Quality and relevance of the methodical and theoretical choices

• 
Consistency and coherence between the research problem and the choice of method and theory

• 
The realistic and feasible scope of the PhD project

• 
Relevance of the project for the DIIS Centre for Peace Research and DIIS in general

Contract and remuneration
The position as PhD candidate starts on 1 February 2027 and is a 3-year full-time position. Remuneration and other job conditions follow the general agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the Danish Ministry of Finance, local collective agreements at DIIS as well as the 28 June 2019 Danish state protocol on PhD candidates. 

The standard starting salary for a PhD candidate at DIIS is 379,702,61 DKK per year excl. pensions – this may be increased depending on prior work experience after the acquisition of the master’s degree. A pension contribution of 18,07% is added to the above-mentioned salary.

Do you want to know more?
Visit http://www.diis.dk/jobs to learn more about DIIS as a workplace. Questions regarding employment and renumeration can be sent to hr@diis.dk. If you have inquiries regarding the professional focus of the position, you can contact Senior Researcher and Head of Research Unit, Mona Kanwal Sheikh at mosh@diis.dk  

The application
Deadline for applying is 23 October 2026, at 12.00 pm CET. 

Please note that we only accept applications through DIIS’ electronic recruitment system. 

Your application must include all the following documents:

• 
A motivational letter

• 
Curriculum Vitae 

• 
Master’s diploma including grades. If you hold a master’s degree which is not within the ECTS-framework, please also provide:

• 
Your bachelor diploma and bachelor grades

• 
A statement clarifying the subject and length (in years) of the master’s degree

• 
An English translation of your diplomas 

• 
PhD project proposal (max 5 pages)

• 
Publication list

DIIS is an independent public research institution for international studies. We conduct and communicate multidisciplinary research on globalisation, security, development and foreign policy and within these areas we aim to be agenda-setting in research, policy and public debate.

DIIS participates in academic networks and publish in high-ranking academic journals, always striving to excel in academic scholarship.

We continuously assess Denmark's foreign and political situation and inform the Danish media, politicians and the public about our work

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in intestinal regeneration and mucosal immunology
jobs.description:
A full-time (100%) postdoctoral position is available in the lab of Dr. Srustidhar Das, at the Department of Clinical Research and at the Research Unit of Inflammation Research, Department of Molecular Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to two years, with the possibility of extension subject to funding.

Research tasks

The position comprises research, teaching, professional development and supervision within intestinal tissue regeneration, epithelial biology, mucosal immunology and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The postdoc will join a translational research programme that investigates how inflammation reshapes the intestinal epithelium and its surrounding tissue niche, and how these changes can be targeted to promote safe and durable mucosal healing.

The successful candidate will combine patient-derived organoid and co-culture models with molecular biology, functional assays, and computational analysis of single-cell and spatial datasets. The position is particularly suited to a researcher who can connect experimental biology with bioinformatics and clinically relevant questions.

Research environment

The postdoc will be embedded in a dynamic and highly collaborative research environment spanning the Department of Clinical Research and the Department of Molecular Medicine at SDU. The project benefits from close interaction among basic scientists, clinicians, bioinformaticians and translational researchers, with strong links to Odense University Hospital and access to patient-derived material, advanced disease models and state-of-the-art molecular technologies.

The environment provides excellent opportunities to develop an independent research profile, contribute to clinically relevant discoveries in IBD and tissue regeneration, and build collaborations across experimental, computational and clinical disciplines.

Research project

The project investigates how inflammatory history establishes persistent epithelial and niche memory, shapes epithelial plasticity and influences intestinal regeneration in IBD. Using patient-derived biopsies, intestinal organoids, fibroblasts and immune-cell co-cultures, we will determine how epithelial memory and injury-induced cell-state transitions influence regenerative capacity and distinguish effective from impaired mucosal healing.

Functional experiments will be integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, chromatin-accessibility analysis, spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics. CRISPR-engineered patient-derived organoids, including lineage reporters and targeted genetic perturbations, will be used to trace epithelial cell states and validate candidate mechanisms. Selected organoids will also be tested in engraftment models to determine whether regenerative phenotypes translate into improved tissue integration and repair in vivo.

Key responsibilities

• 
Establish and manipulate patient-derived intestinal organoids and fibroblast–immune-cell co-cultures to investigate epithelial plasticity, cell-state transitions, regeneration, inflammatory responses and barrier function.

• 
Generate and validate CRISPR-engineered organoids, including reporter lines and targeted genetic perturbations, and perform engraftment studies to assess regenerative potential in vivo.

• 
Analyse and integrate scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomic and spatial epigenomic datasets using reproducible workflows for quality control, differential analysis, cell-state annotation, trajectory analysis and multimodal integration.

• 
Apply molecular and cellular methods, including qPCR, immunostaining, advanced microscopy, flow cytometry and ELISA-based assays, and validate candidate pathways using pharmacological and CRISPR-based perturbations where appropriate.

• 
Collaborate with clinicians, experimental scientists and bioinformaticians to analyse and interpret patient-derived samples and data.

• 
Maintain accurate and reproducible records, present findings, prepare manuscripts and conference contributions, and contribute to grant applications, teaching and supervision where relevant.

Expectations of qualifications

The successful applicant must hold a PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, immunology, bioinformatics, computational biology, regenerative medicine, biomedicine or a closely related discipline, with documented research experience relevant to the project.

Essential qualifications

• 
Documented experience in organoid biology, preferably involving intestinal or other tissue-derived epithelial organoids, and in designing mechanistic studies of epithelial plasticity and regeneration.

• 
A strong background in tissue regeneration, epithelial biology, mucosal immunology, inflammatory disease or a closely related field.

• 
Demonstrated expertise in analysing single-cell or spatial-omics data, with proficiency in R and/or Python and experience developing reproducible computational workflows.

• 
Hands-on experience in molecular and cell biology, with the ability to design, perform, troubleshoot and interpret experiments using a structured and careful approach to data analysis, documentation and responsible research practice.

• 
A strong publication record appropriate to career stage; excellent written and spoken English; and the ability to drive projects independently while collaborating effectively in a multidisciplinary and international environment.

Desirable qualifications

• 
Experience with intestinal organoids, patient-derived material, fibroblast or immune-cell culture, or epithelial–stromal–immune co-culture models.

• 
Experience integrating scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomic, spatial epigenomic or other multimodal datasets.

• 
Familiarity with advanced imaging, quantitative image analysis, flow cytometry, organoid phenotyping or high-content screening.

• 
Demonstrated experience generating and validating CRISPR-engineered organoids, including knock-in reporters or targeted gene perturbations, and with intestinal organoid engraftment or transplantation and in vivo assessment of epithelial regeneration is highly preferred.

• 
An interest in supervising junior researchers and contributing to collaborative teaching and research activities.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

jobs.occupation: Software Tester & Quality Specialist – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition
jobs.description:
Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time. 

Based in Copenhagen, Nordic RCC is one of six RCCs in Europe, equally owned by the Nordic region's four electricity TSOs: Fingrid, Statnett, Svenska Kraftnät, and Energinet. 

As European power systems integrate and evolve to meet climate goals, Nordic RCC provides regional coordination, integrated services, regional insights and recommendations to the Nordic TSOs and their control centres, to support cross-border operational security 24/7.  

Join Nordic RCC, a fast-developing company determined to make a significant impact in the energy sector and to provide for a secure and efficient transition to the green, sustainable energy system. 

Right now, we are looking for a Software Tester & Quality Specialist who likes to make a difference! 

Job description: 

As a Software Tester & Quality Specialist in the Quality Management team, you will work closely with developers, business experts, product owners, project managers, test managers, and fellow testers to help ensure the quality of Nordic RCC's systems and services.

We believe quality starts long before testing begins. Therefore, you will be involved early in the development process, helping teams identify risks, clarify requirements, and prepare testing activities before solutions are implemented. We are in the progress of strengthening our processes and “shifting-left” to achieve this target state.

You will contribute throughout the development lifecycle by reviewing acceptance criteria, creating test data, designing and executing tests, supporting business and operators is test decision and execution, and communicating test results and quality concerns. By working closely with both business and development teams, you will help ensure that quality is built into our solutions from the start.

Your key responsibilities are:

• 
Work closely with developers, business experts, product owners, project managers, test managers, and fellow testers throughout the development lifecycle.

• 
Participate in requirement reviews, refinement sessions, and solution discussions to identify risks, gaps, and testing needs as early as possible.

• 
Help ensure that testing considerations are included early in development activities and that quality is addressed before implementation is completed.

• 
Review requirements, user stories, and solution designs to identify potential risks, gaps, and ambiguities.

• 
Identify dependencies, prerequisites, and test data requirements for testing activities.

• 
Create, maintain, and analyse test data to support testing across different systems and environments.

• 
Design, maintain, and execute test cases and test scenarios based on business and technical requirements.

• 
Perform manual and exploratory testing to verify functionality, usability, integrations, and business processes.

• 
Identify, document, and follow up on defects and quality issues in collaboration with development teams and business stakeholders.

• 
Support investigation and root cause analysis of defects and recurring quality issues.

• 
Contribute test cases, effort estimates, dependencies, and risks as input to test planning activities.

• 
Document and communicate test results, findings, and quality concerns to support project and test management reporting.

• 
Collaborate with developers and test automation specialists to improve testing practices and automated quality controls.

• 
Contribute to the continuous improvement of testing methods, test data practices, and quality assurance processes across Nordic RCC.

Proactive position with outstanding attention to detail and excellent communication skills 

On the personal level you have attention to details, good communication and collaboration skills, analytical thinking and problem solving. You are a self-driven and proactive person, responsible, structured and have a strong focus on finding a solution to the problems at hand.

The ideal candidate is expected to have a minimum of 5 years in manual test experience, an education at BA or MA level in computer science or engineering, but experience from a similar role is more important.

Technical skills: 

• 
Collaborate with internal and external development teams in the CI/CD process. 

• 
Strong knowledge of software QA methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, etc), tools, processes, and development cycles (SDLC). 

• 
Experience with test data creation

• 
Good understanding of test automation

Preferred Qualifications: 

• 
ISTQB certification or equivalent 

• 
Experience with test management tools - Azure DevOps, Jira, etc. 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet all the listed requirements.

Employment conditions 

You will join a team of competent, diverse, and enthusiastic colleagues. We are currently 22 nationalities with more than 30% women (striving to improve this balance) and all ages.

Your daily workplace will be in our office premises in Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad. We are offering workplace flexibility to ensure a healthy work-life balance including the possibility for working from home some of your worktime. 

Our values of fellowship, curiosity, respect, and transparency have been defined by all employees. They identify how we behave and shape the way we work together, and we expect you to see yourself in them.

Note: The position is conditioned upon a satisfactory background check as well as a national security clearance, both of which will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note, that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.

Application deadline and contact information

Please apply online as soon as possible (in English) and no later than 1st November 2026. We may conduct interviews on a continuous basis.

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system. 

If you have any questions, please contact Håkon Rosenaa Nystad, Manager, Quality Management, hny@nordic-rcc.net.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Veterinary Microbiology
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

   

  We are looking for an experienced and highly motivated veterinary microbiologist for a 2-year part-time postdoc position starting around 1st January 2027. The new postdoc is expected to contribute to the scientific and teaching activities of the research group One Health Antimicrobial Resistance (OHAR) within the section of Veterinary Clinical Microbiology. Additionally, the postdoc will be responsible for defined scientific and management activities within the project SOA36 - Designing best veterinary practices to reduce antimicrobial and antiparasitic use (BEST-VET), funded by the European Partnership on Animal Health and Welfare (EUPAHW). These responsibilities include supporting the project Chair in the day-to-day coordination and management of the consortium, as well as planning and conducting research aimed at reducing antimicrobial use in pigs through improved diagnostic and treatment protocols for key endemic bacterial diseases, and active involvement in the development of clinical guidelines for prudent antimicrobial use in pig medicine, with a particular focus on developing evidence-based guidelines using the GRADE approach. Through these activities, the postdoc will contribute to strengthening antimicrobial stewardship and promoting evidence-based best practices in veterinary medicine.

  Information on the department and the section can be found at: https://ivh.ku.dk/.

  Our research
 The postdoc will be part of the OHAR research group led by Prof. Luca Guardabassi. Our research is characterized by two focus areas:

   	
• Development of diagnostic tests and methods to reduce and rationalize antimicrobial use in animals. 	
• Optimization of veterinary antimicrobial use to minimize selection and spread of antimicrobial resistance.   For more information, please check the OHAR homepage One Health Antimicrobial Resistance (OHAR) – University of Copenhagen

  Your job
 You are a highly qualified veterinary microbiologist with the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team. You will be required to be physically present in the laboratory to contribute to ongoing research projects and oversee experiments conducted by PhD, MSc, and BSc students. As part of the EU project BEST-VET, you will contribute to selected work packages and expert groups, including WP1 (Reduction of drug use in pigs), WP7 (Environmental impact of antimicrobial/antiparasitic drugs and phage therapy), Expert Group 1 (Phages and their environmental impact), Expert Group 3 (Standardization of sampling, metagenomics & analytical methods) and Expert Group 5 (Clinical guidance). You will be responsible for coordinating and following up on SOA36 activities related to these work packages and expert groups. You will also act as a key point of contact between the project management, work package leaders and expert groups. Your project management responsibilities will further include supporting the organisation of Management Board meetings, following up on project activities and deadlines, and maintaining the SOA36 SharePoint and associated project documentation. As part of the position, you will undertake a one-year training programme in evidence-based guideline development using the GRADE approach and subsequently contribute to the development of evidence-based clinical guidelines for veterinary medicine.

  Profile 
 We are seeking a highly qualified scientist with a strong track record of independent research in veterinary bacteriology and experience in international collaborative research project coordination, as well as in the supervision and teaching of veterinary and postgraduate students.

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• A MSc degree in Veterinary Medicine 	
• A PhD in Veterinary Microbiology or a closely related field 	
• Previous postdoctoral experience 	
• Outstanding publication record in relation to career stage 	
• Excellent scientific writing and oral communication skills 	
• Experience in supervising PhD, MSc, and BSc students 	
• Experience in the coordination and management of collaborative research projects 	
• Experience with bacterial whole-genome sequencing and genomic data analysis 	
• Knowledge of key concepts in antimicrobial stewardship   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Research experience in antimicrobial resistance 	
• Experience in metagenomics 	
• Experience in routine bacteriological and mycological diagnostics 	
• Experience in preparing research proposals and applications for external funding   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories that are fully equipped to perform traditional and molecular microbiology, including omics.

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 per week.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Questions
 For further information please contact Luca Guardabassi (lg@sund.ku.dk).

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers   After the expiry date or applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Application deadline: 15 October 2026, 23.59 CEST.

  Interviews are expected to be held in weeks 44-45 (26th October – 5th November 2026).

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone.

jobs.occupation: Sales Executive  - Ready to turn Software/ERP expertise into closed deals? Interform HQ Birkerød, DK or Remote
jobs.description:
The role

Interform builds InterformNG2, an Output Management platform that sits next to the ERP and handles the documents a business runs on: invoices, labels, delivery notes, e-invoicing. When output fails, shipments stop and invoices get rejected. Our customers buy certainty that this never happens.

You will sell InterformNG2 to new customers across Europe - with our core markets in the Nordics, Germany and Austria, Benelux and the UK - typically manufacturing, logistics and distribution companies running ERPs such as Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or IBM i. You own the full sales cycle from first conversation to signed agreement.

There is no BDR team here, but you are not starting from a blank sheet either. We identify the most relevant accounts together, backed by an AI-driven engine that tracks buying signals across our markets. Your job is what happens next: the outreach, the conversations, the proposals and the close.

What you will do

• 
Turn qualified target accounts into meetings, pipeline and closed deals across your European territory.

• 
Open doors through direct outreach and your own network of ERP consultants, partners and IT decision-makers.

• 
Run full sales cycles - qualification, demo coordination, proposal, negotiation, close - in close collaboration with the rest of the commercial team.

• 
Work with our partner ecosystem around Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, IBM i and other ERP platforms as a second route to market.

• 
Feed what you learn in the market back into how we position and price.

Who you are

• 
Driven. You show up every day ready to do your best, and you keep that standard through long sales cycles.

• 
Connected in the ERP ecosystem. Ecosystem knowledge is essential in this role: you know at least one major ERP ecosystem in real depth - the partners and implementation consultants in it, how they influence a deal and when to bring them in - and you bring a working network you can call on from day one.

• 
Self-starting. You plan your own work, execute without being chased, and deliver.

• 
Accountable. You own your number and you follow up - customers can trust that you are always a step ahead.

• 
At home in the ERP world. You have sold software or services into environments running Infor, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, IBM i or comparable ERP platforms, and you speak the language of IT managers and operations directors.

• 
AI-forward. You already use AI in your daily sales work - research, preparation, follow-up - and want a company that works the same way.

• 
A closer. You have proven you can turn outreach into pipeline and pipeline into signed deals - not just manage inbound.

• 
Languages: fluent English is required. German, Danish or Dutch on top is a strong advantage - ideally you cover one of our core markets natively.

What we offer

• 
A place in a solid company: profitable, in strong growth, and with a large market still ahead of us.

• 
A product that is easy to stand behind: more than 4,500 installations worldwide, and customers who stay.

• 
A defined category - Output Management - where we compete on depth, not noise.

• 
Short decision paths and direct access to management.

• 
An AI-driven account-based marketing engine that shows you which companies are in the market - so your time goes to conversations, not list-building.

• 
A competitive package that rewards what you close.

About Interform A/S

Interform has built Output Management software since 1987 from our headquarters in Birkerød, Denmark. Our platform, InterformNG2, works with any ERP, any format and any environment - customers change or upgrade their ERP and keep their output running. Our first customer from 1987 is still with us today. Our customer base is international - companies across the Nordics, Germany and Austria, Benelux, the UK and further afield - and our own team works across borders in the same way, with colleagues based in Denmark and Germany. We are a profitable, solidly run company in strong growth, and investment backing supports continued development of the platform.

Practical details

• 
Location: our office in Birkerød, Denmark, or remote from anywhere in our European markets - we already have employees working outside Denmark, so a distributed setup is nothing new to us.

• 
Travel: limited. Most sales work runs remotely, with occasional customer, partner and event travel.

• 
Reports to: our Chief Commercial Officer - you will work alongside the rest of the commercial team.

• 
Start: as soon as possible. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

How to apply

Upload your CV and cover letter, including the deals you are most proud of.

Birkerød I Remote

Opportunities to influence product security strategies in real-world projects.

About Prevas: Engineering Excellence in Embedded Linux & Electronics

We see development as a natural part of life – from idea to product, and from career to personal growth. Our open, inclusive atmosphere provides you with the space to be yourself and develop your ideas, while working across disciplines with dedicated colleagues.

If you share our passion for problem-solving, teamwork, and learning, and you want to help shape the future of embedded systems and secure IoT solutions, we’d love to hear from you.

Contact Us

We look forward to welcoming you to Prevas – where every day is a chance to build something great together.
